messages:
maria: noticed a strange window where a prefix stayed served after a lease handoff — node-b kept serving for ~18s.

maria: sequencer shows lease granted to node-a at 09:11:02 but node-b logged continued serving until 09:11:20. suspect the demote signal didn't reach observers.

ben: do we know if delta stream laged or if the demote event was dropped by the watcher?

maria: delta stream lag. node-b's delta consumer lagged behind and never applied the demote tombstone.

sam: can we make demote signals more robust? what about writing a lightweight monotonic demote-counter to control so late replicas can reconcile?

dana: that reduces dependence on timely streaming. but we should avoid adding latency to handoffs. maybe async write + best-effort fanout.

kevin: alternative: sample reads for verification. on a small fraction of reads, compare local epoch to control epoch; if mismatch, trigger a fast local demote. low write overhead, some read overhead.

ben: both approaches are complementary. counter write gives eventual correctness; read-sampling gives faster detection without too many control writes.

maria: implementation idea: on_handoff -> control.write_demote_counter(prefix, epoch) (async). on_read -> with p=0.01 read control.counter(prefix) and fast_demote if mismatch. also add idempotent tombstone apply.

dana: add telemetry: per-prefix demote-latency histogram and a metric 'serve_claim_epoch' vs 'last_applied_demote_epoch' per node. alert when delta > 5s.

kevin: also propose observer-heartbeat metric {node,prefix,epoch,last_applied_seq}. if node says serving but heartbeat shows stale seq for > Xs, trigger a demote-probe and optionally route reads via sequencer until healed.

sam: note: control reads on-hot path must be non-blocking. do verification asynchronously and make demote a best-effort mark that doesn't block reads.

ben: ensure demote counter is idempotent and monotonic so reordering won't resurrect a prefix. tombstone vector should be compact to stream.

maria: ok. i'll draft an RFC: demote-counter async writes + probabilistic read verification + observer-heartbeat telemetry + fallback sequencer-routing > 30s. who wants to co-author?

dana: i'll take telemetry/alerts.

ben: i'll own counter writes and idempotent apply.

sam: i'll prototype probabilistic read-sampling.

maria: thanks. filing this thread for tracking.
